name: Turgor Exam Engine
author: turgorlabs

sections.description:
Turgor Exam Engine is a full LMS for WordPress, built around competitive-exam style tests. Run mock tests with negative marking, timed papers in sections and numeric-range answers, and build the courses that lead up to them, all on your own WordPress site and database – not a hosted service.

Made for coaching institutes, test-series sellers and teachers preparing students for exams like SSC, IBPS, JEE, NEET, GATE and CSIR NET.

Exam engine

  • Eight question types: single choice, multiple choice, fill in the blank, free answer (which can accept a numeric range – an answer key of “6300..6400”, as GATE and IIT JAM publish), sorting, matching, rating scale and essay. Seven are marked automatically; essays wait on the Results screen for a teacher to mark.
  • Negative marking, with a per-question penalty where a paper needs one.
  • Standalone mock tests: open any quiz to every signed-in student from its own page, no course needed.
  • Timed papers split into named sections, with retake limits and question and answer shuffling. (A separate timer per section is part of Exam Mode in Turgor Exam Engine Pro.)
  • A question bank with categories, difficulty levels and topics: search it, filter it and edit any question, and every quiz that uses it changes with it.
  • A Results screen listing every attempt, where you mark essays, give a student their retakes back, or re-mark attempts after correcting an answer key.
  • Sitewide defaults for every setting, overridable on any single quiz.
  • A per-question review after submission, and a results chart students can see with [turgee_quiz_results].
  • Random questions: a section draws questions from a question-bank category, so every student gets a different paper.
  • Live tests with open and close times: nobody starts outside the window, and anyone still sitting the quiz is stopped at closing time.
  • Question analysis on Results: right, wrong and blank counts per question and the average time, hardest first.
  • Reading passages shared by several questions, and LaTeX formulae drawn as typeset maths.
  • Choose when students see the right answers: straight away, when no attempts are left, after the quiz closes, or never.

Courses

Build each course as an outline of sections, topics, lessons, sub-lessons and quizzes. Drag items into place or use the + buttons, create a lesson or quiz by typing its title, and set prerequisites and completion rules per course. Students see the same outline on the course page.

  • Drip content: a lesson or quiz opens a set number of days after access begins, and/or not before a date.
  • Assignments, marked with a mark and feedback, and lesson discussions using ordinary WordPress comments.
  • Lesson videos with chapters, a speed menu and resume.
  • Gutenberg blocks and shortcodes for course lists, quizzes, progress, results and sign-in.
  • Open, no-signup courses and one-click free enrollment.
  • A Quick start checklist and a one-click sample course to get a new site running.
  • An Instructor role that can mark essays and see results without being an administrator.

Already running LearnDash?

A guided import brings your courses, lessons, quizzes and enrolled students across, with verification tools that check the migration actually worked before you switch over – nothing is deleted or changed on your live site until you say so.

Want to sell what you build?

Turgor Exam Engine is free and complete on its own. Turgor Exam Engine Pro adds Exam Mode (the computer-based exam screen, with a timer per section and partial marks for multiple choice), WooCommerce and Google Play Billing checkout, bundled Products (and, when moving from LearnDash, bringing groups, bundles and WooCommerce products across, with checks that paid courses moved over correctly), class reports, certificates issued automatically on completion, copy protection for lesson and quiz content, and student feedback tools. Pro is one purchase that includes all of it, and it is never required: everything in Turgor Exam Engine works fully without it.

Requirements

  • PHP 8.1 or newer
  • WordPress 6.7 or newer

Third-party libraries

  • KaTeX 0.16.11, MIT License – draws formulae in questions. Bundled minified as assets/vendor/katex/katex.min.js and auto-render.min.js, with its stylesheet and fonts; the source is at https://github.com/KaTeX/KaTeX.
  • Chart.js 4.5.1, MIT License – draws the quiz-results chart. Bundled minified as assets/vendor/chart.umd.min.js; the unminified source is at https://github.com/chartjs/Chart.js.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin files to /wp-content/plugins/turgor-exam-engine, or install the zip directly through Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin.
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins screen.
  3. Open Turgor Exam Engine in the wp-admin sidebar to create your first course, or go to Turgor Exam Engine → Migration (shown once LearnDash is active) if you’re moving off LearnDash.
sections.faq:
Do I need LearnDash installed to use this?

No. Turgor Exam Engine is a standalone course platform and works with no other LMS plugin present. LearnDash support exists specifically for sites migrating away from it.

Will migrating from LearnDash delete my existing LearnDash data?

No. The import reads your existing LearnDash content and copies it into Turgor Exam Engine’s own tables; nothing is deleted, and LearnDash can stay active and serving your site right up until you choose to switch over.

Can I sell courses with the free plugin?

Course access rules (open, free enrollment, restricted) are included free. Selling courses for payment – WooCommerce, subscriptions, or Google Play Billing – requires Turgor Exam Engine Pro.

Where do I report a bug or ask for help?

https://turgorlabs.com/documentation/complete-guide/

Which shortcodes are there?

  • [turgee_quiz id="123"] – the quiz player for quiz 123 (on a quiz’s own page, id can be left out).
  • [turgee_quiz_results] – the signed-in student’s score history as a chart.
  • [turgee_course_progress course_id="123"] – a course’s progress bar.
  • [turgee_course_content course_id="123"] – a course’s lesson and quiz list.
  • [turgee_breadcrumbs] – Course > Lesson > Topic > Quiz trail on any of those pages.
  • [turgee_login] – a sign-in form, with lost-password and reset-password screens.
  • [turgee_login] also offers student sign-up, and Sign in links open a popup.
  • [turgee_login_button] – a Sign in (or Create account) button that opens the popup. Options: label, view="login|signup", class, redirect. A menu item or link to #turgor-login or #turgor-signup opens the popup too (needs JavaScript and the popup on).
  • Sign-in, sign-up and password-reset attempts are limited per visitor IP address (10 attempts in 15 minutes), so many people behind one shared address (a school lab) can hit the limit; the turgee_auth_rate_limit filter raises it.
  • [turgee_profile] – the signed-in student’s profile: quiz stats, activity, their courses with progress, and scores over time.
  • [turgee_if_logged_in]...[/turgee_if_logged_in] and [turgee_if_logged_out]...[/turgee_if_logged_out] – show the enclosed content only to signed-in or signed-out visitors.

  • [turgee_courses] – a grid of your published courses, with lesson count, whether each is free, and the student’s own progress. Options: limit="12", orderby="menu_order|title|date", order="ASC|DESC". With Turgor Exam Engine Pro, this becomes the Pro storefront (bundles and prices).

  • [turgee_quizzes] – a grid of your standalone mock tests (quizzes with “Open to every signed-in student” ticked), with question count, time limit, negative marking and the student’s best score. Options: limit="12", orderby="date|title|menu_order", order="ASC|DESC".

All published courses are also listed at /courses/ on a new site.

How do I add videos to a lesson?

Use the Lesson videos box on the lesson or topic editor. Each video has an address (choose an MP4 from the media library), an optional title and poster image, and optional chapters, one per line, such as 1:54 Exam summary.

A lesson can have several videos, one for each subtopic. Each video has a tag such as [turgee_video n="2"]. Paste the tag into the lesson text where that video should play, under its subtopic’s heading for example. A video whose tag is not in the text plays above the lesson. Each player has a chapter list, a speed menu and resume, and starting one video pauses the others.

To keep paid videos on a CDN that only hands out signed, expiring links (Bunny CDN), use Turgor Exam Engine Pro’s video hosting.

Can every student get a different set of questions?

Yes. In the quiz editor, under Random questions, choose a category of your question bank and how many questions to draw. Each attempt is drawn once when the student starts, so resuming keeps the same questions. A section that draws replaces the questions you placed in it; other sections stay as they are.

Can I run a live test that opens and closes at set times?

Yes. Set Opens and Closes in the quiz editor. Nobody can start outside that window, and a student still sitting the quiz at closing time is stopped then, so everyone finishes together and a late starter gets less time.

How do I find questions that are too hard or wrongly marked?

Open Results, choose a quiz, and click Question analysis. It lists every question with how many students got it right, wrong or left it blank, hardest first. A question almost nobody gets right is worth checking against its answer key.

What happens to my data if I delete the plugin?

Nothing, by default: the results, progress and settings stay in your database, so reinstalling brings them back. To remove them, switch on When the plugin is deleted under Turgor Exam Engine > Settings before deleting. That deletes the plugin’s tables and settings (including Turgor Exam Engine Pro’s products and access records, which share them). Courses, lessons and quizzes stay as ordinary posts.

Can a student ask for their data, or for it to be erased?

Yes. The plugin adds itself to Tools > Export Personal Data and Tools > Erase Personal Data. Erasing removes their attempts, answers, progress, time and feedback; records of purchases are kept for your accounts, and the tool says so.

Can a tutor mark essays without being an administrator?

Yes. Give them the Instructor role. It can write courses, lessons and quizzes, and see Results, mark essays and reset retakes for the quizzes it wrote (not other people’s), but cannot change site settings.

Does this plugin contact any external service?

No. Turgor Exam Engine makes no requests to outside servers. A lesson video plays from the address you entered for it, loaded by the student’s browser or app, not by the plugin. Links to the documentation and to Turgor Exam Engine Pro on turgorlabs.com are ordinary links that only open when you click them. The video guide on the overview page loads from YouTube (youtube-nocookie.com) only after you press its play button.
sections.changelog:
0.9.1

  • Fixed: the “My quiz results” chart was blank on pages built with the plugin’s blocks, including the page made by “Create the standard pages”. It now draws.
  • Fixed: a Sign in page built with the Sign-in form block is now found as your site’s sign-in page, so Sign in links and password-reset emails point at it.
  • Fixed: a quiz that already holds the Quiz block no longer gets a second quiz player added under it.
  • New: a video guide on the overview page – a full walk-through of the plugin. It loads from YouTube only when you press play.
  • New: a “Rate this plugin” link on the Plugins screen, and one polite, dismissible request for a WordPress.org review on the Turgor overview page after two weeks of use. “Maybe later” and “I already did” both stop it.

0.9.0

  • Security: a lesson’s text can no longer be read by someone who is not enrolled through the WordPress REST API, the site’s feeds or its search results. Only the lesson’s own page checked before.
  • Security: in the question bank a question can be changed or deleted only by whoever wrote it, or by an editor or administrator. Questions that came from an import are for editors and administrators only.
  • Security: signing in is limited per account as well as per address, a sign-up that succeeds no longer counts against the address limit, and sites behind Cloudflare or another proxy can tell the plugin the visitor’s real address.
  • Security: time-spent pings need access to the lesson and cannot be sent in a loop to inflate reports.
  • New: choose when students see the right answers after a quiz – straight away (as before), only when no attempts are left, only after the quiz closes, or never. Set a site default on Quiz Settings and change it on any quiz.
  • New: optionally let Instructors edit each other’s courses, lessons, sub-lessons, quizzes and question-bank questions. Off by default.
  • New: a lesson a student cannot open now links to its course page.
  • Changed: the Pro upgrade page shows a Free and Pro comparison and a short list of questions. No prices are shown in the plugin.
  • Changed: development packages (the test tools) now install on PHP 8.1 and later.

0.8.3

  • Fixed: on a brand-new install WordPress 6.7+ logged a “translation loaded too early” notice when the plugin was first activated. The Instructor role is now set up on init.
  • Fixed: the Assignments screen showed a huge check icon when empty, because it did not load the plugin’s admin styles.
  • Fixed: the Welcome screen no longer puts the Pro card above your own status when the window is narrow.
  • Fixed: assignment answer box and Submit button now look like the rest of the lesson page.
  • Changed: lessons, sub-lessons, quizzes and courses support an author, so “Written by” shows a name and the author can be chosen in the editor.
  • Changed: the course outline is easier to build. Section, Topic and quiz buttons sit above it; items in the Add content panel can be dragged into the outline (drop left or right to choose the level); the selected row is clearly marked; and a one-line how-to is shown.
  • Fixed: the all-courses page (/courses/) showed the theme’s plain list of titles. It now shows the course grid, with your theme’s header and footer. Turn it off with the filter turgee_course_archive_grid.
  • Changed: the course outline now shows its hierarchy: every item is a box that steps in with its level, with a coloured edge per type and a curved connector line from its parent, so you can see at a glance what sits under what.
  • New: a “This lesson” box at the top of a lesson’s sidebar lists what the lesson has switched on (release rule, assignment, videos, discussion).
  • Fixed: in a narrow editor the course outline no longer squeezes lesson titles into a few letters per line.
  • Changed: the question form asks for the answers before the optional category, difficulty and topic.

0.8.2

  • New: the course and quiz screens warn before you leave with changes that are not saved.
  • New: quiz questions have Move up and Move down buttons, so a paper can be reordered with a keyboard or a finger.
  • Changed: the Welcome screen starts with your Quick start checklist; the feature tour, Free vs Pro and shortcode list are folded below it.
  • Changed: a new quiz can have sections named before its first save, and says plainly that nothing is saved until you press Publish or Save draft.
  • Changed: Paid and Subscription are switched off in the course Access box until Pro can sell the course, and the wording no longer points at a menu that is not there.
  • Changed: the page inside a lesson is always called a sub-lesson; Topic is the heading between a section and its lessons.
  • Changed: the course screen says how to write a lesson (its Edit link).

0.8.1

  • New: a Quick start checklist on the Welcome screen that ticks itself as you create a course, a lesson and a quiz.
  • New: Create a sample course adds a small course (two lessons and a three-question quiz) so you can see how it fits together, then change or delete it.
  • New: Create the standard pages adds Courses, Sign in, My account and My quiz results pages using the plugin’s blocks.

0.8.0

  • New: drip content. A lesson, sub-lesson or quiz can open a number of days after a student’s access began, and/or not before a date. Set it in the Release box on the lesson. A student with access sees when it opens.
  • New: assignments. Turn a lesson or sub-lesson into an assignment in its Assignment box. Students write an answer and can rewrite it until it is marked; you mark it under Assignments with a mark and feedback. Instructors mark only assignments on lessons they wrote.
  • New: lesson discussions. Students can comment under each lesson they have access to. These are ordinary WordPress comments, so your moderation and spam settings apply. Turn it on under Settings.
  • New: emails when a student completes a course and when an assignment is marked, with editable text.
  • New: Gutenberg blocks for the course list, quiz list, a quiz, course progress, course contents, quiz results, profile, sign-in form and breadcrumbs.
  • For developers: filter turgee_drip_release_at; actions turgee_assignment_submitted and turgee_assignment_graded.

0.7.1

  • New: reading passages. Give several questions the same passage (a text, a table, a diagram) and students see it above each of them. Type a passage title in the question editor; questions with the same title share the same text.
  • New: formulae. Write LaTeX between \( and \) (inline) or between \[ and \] or $$ and $$ (on its own line) in a question, an answer or a passage and it is drawn as typeset math. A single $ is not a formula marker, so prices are safe. The maths library loads only on a quiz that uses it.

  • New: true or false as a question type in the question editor. It is saved as a two-option single-choice question.

  • Improved: answers given on a poor connection. A failed save is sent again the moment the connection returns, and closing the tab with an answer not yet saved asks first.

0.7.0

  • New: random questions. A quiz section can draw a number of questions at random from one category of the question bank, so every student gets a different paper. Set it up in the quiz editor under Random questions. A section that draws replaces the questions placed in it, and a category with fewer questions than you ask for gives all it has.
  • New: open and close times on a quiz, for live tests. Nobody can start outside them, and anyone still sitting the quiz when it closes is stopped at closing time, so a late starter gets less time. Times are entered in your site’s timezone.
  • New: Question analysis on Results: for one quiz, how many students had each question, how many got it right, wrong or left it blank, and the average time. The hardest question comes first.
  • For developers: filters turgee_pool_candidates, turgee_quiz_window, turgee_question_analysis_columns and turgee_question_analysis_row.

0.6.0

  • New: Instructor role. Tutors can see the Results of the quizzes they wrote, mark essays and reset retakes without being administrators. Two new capabilities, turgee_view_results and turgee_grade, do the gating; administrators have both.
  • New: Export CSV on Results, for the quiz, student and status you are looking at.
  • New: works with WordPress’s Export / Erase Personal Data tools: quiz attempts and answers, course progress, time on lessons, ratings and reports. Deleting a user erases the same data. Purchase records are kept, and the tool says so.
  • New: When the plugin is deleted setting. Off by default; switched on, deleting the plugin also deletes its tables, settings and the Instructor role. Courses, lessons and quizzes are kept as posts.
  • Changed: Results now needs turgee_view_results instead of manage_options. Administrators are unaffected.
  • For developers: filters turgee_lms_instructor_caps, turgee_results_see_all, turgee_results_export_columns and turgee_results_export_row.

0.5.5

  • Fixed: opening the Migration screen no longer logs a PHP deprecation notice under WP_DEBUG.

0.5.4

  • Changed: clean pass of the official Plugin Check – explicit query arguments and a version on the brand style handle.

0.5.3

  • Fixed: a request-method check now unslashes and sanitizes its input; escaping and documentation touch-ups found in a code-standards pass.

0.5.2

  • Changed: the brand colour variables are now added with WordPress’s own style queue (wp_add_inline_style) instead of a hand-printed style tag.

0.5.1

  • Fixed: a direct-access guard on one REST handler file.

0.5.0

  • New: tile layout for the course page and lessons, a brand colour setting, and a clearer quiz player (palette, flags, in-page submit dialog, retry on failed saves).
  • New: lesson video hooks that Turgor Exam Engine Pro’s Video add-on uses for captions and resume.
  • Changed: the plugin now states the oldest Turgor Exam Engine Pro it works with and ignores an older one.
  • Changed: the Documentation link opens the complete guide.

0.4.0

  • New: four more question types – sorting (put items in order), matching (pair each item with its match), rating scale (each point earns its own score) and essay (marked by a teacher). All eight question types can now be written and taken.
  • New: Questions screen – the whole question bank in one place. Search it, filter by category, difficulty and type, and edit any question; every quiz that uses it changes with it.
  • New: Results screen – every quiz attempt. Mark essays, give a student their retakes back, or re-mark attempts after correcting an answer key.
  • New: sections in a quiz, such as Reasoning and Quantitative Aptitude. Students see each section’s title over its questions, and shuffling stays within a section.
  • Changed: quiz time limits are entered in minutes.
  • Fixed: a quiz created in WordPress ignored the sitewide Quiz Settings; new quizzes now follow them.
  • Fixed: quiz settings are checked before saving, so a value like “abc” is refused instead of quietly becoming 0.
  • Fixed: typing a quiz setting while “Use site default” was ticked threw the value away.
  • Fixed: a question written in a quiz that failed to save was lost; it now comes back filled in.
  • Fixed: on Settings, the Google Play Billing card (with Turgor Exam Engine Pro) was squeezed into a narrow column and its fields and help text were cut off at the edge. It now takes the full width.
  • New: a Settings link next to Deactivate on the Plugins screen.
  • New: the app can open a course or lesson link from your website on its own screen (turgee/v1/resolve-link).
  • Moving from LearnDash? Run the question import again to bring matching and rating-scale questions across with their pairs and scores.

0.3.12

  • New: every answer option in the question composer has an Add image button, so options can be pictures – figure series, diagrams, graphs. It works on rows added with “Add another answer” too.
  • Fixed: an answer option that was only an image was dropped when the question was saved.
  • Fixed: My courses could show a course as “4 of 0 lessons” after 0.3.11 when the live lesson count came back empty; it now falls back to the saved count.
  • Fixed: two submits of the same quiz arriving together (a double-tap, an app retry) could both send the result email. Only the first one counts now, and the second gets the same result back.
  • Fixed: two starts of the same quiz at the same moment could open two papers and let a student go past the quiz’s attempt limit.

0.3.11

  • Fixed: My courses showed “0 of 0 lessons” for a course the student had not started yet. It now shows the course’s real number of lessons.

0.3.10

  • New: every Google Play unlock attempt is now recorded, not only the ones that succeeded, so Turgor Exam Engine Pro’s Orders screen can show a student stuck mid-purchase. (0.3.9 sites get the new table on update.)

0.3.9

  • New: lesson videos. The Lesson videos box on the lesson and topic editor sets any number of videos, each with a title, poster and chapters. Place each one in the lesson text with its [turgee_video n="2"] tag; one without a tag plays above the lesson. Players have a chapter list, a speed menu and resume. The app gets the videos from lessons/{id}.
  • New: lessons?course= and the course outline say which lessons have a video (has_video), never where.
  • Changed: the quiz builder’s “Bulk import questions from CSV” box is removed. Importing whole papers from Excel, CSV, Word and Google Sheets is Turgor Exam Engine Pro’s Quiz Toolkit. Questions you already imported stay as they are.
  • For developers: turgee_lesson_video_url filters the URL a student is given for a video; Turgor Exam Engine Pro’s video hosting uses it to sign CDN links.

0.3.8

  • New: Topics – group lessons under a topic inside a section, or directly in the course. Quizzes can sit in the course, a section, a topic, a lesson or a sub-lesson. The pages inside a lesson are now called Sub-lessons.
  • New: drag a lesson or quiz into a section, topic or lesson in the course builder; move the pointer left or right while dragging to step out or in a level.
  • New: the course page shows each section once, with its topics, lessons and quizzes nested under it and a count of what each holds.
  • New: create lessons, sub-lessons and quizzes straight from the course page, and open any of them for editing in a new tab.
  • New: GET turgee/v1/courses/{id}/outline returns a course as a tree – sections, topics, lessons, sub-lessons and every quiz – for apps.
  • Changed: every REST API route is served under turgee/v1 (and turgee-dashboard/v1) on every site, with nothing to switch on first. The Migration screen’s “Switch the site over” step is gone, and on a site moved from LearnDash, quizzes work as soon as the content is copied.
  • Fixed: a passed quiz is ticked as done on the course page.
  • Changed: Elementor widgets are named turgee-course-content, turgee-course-infobar and turgee-profile. Sites moved from LearnDash also keep LearnDash’s widget names so their templates keep working.
  • Fixed: a question without its own title no longer shows its text twice, on the quiz or in the quiz builder.
  • Changed: on a site that never used LearnDash, courses, lessons, topics and quizzes use this plugin’s own content types. Sites moved from LearnDash keep theirs, so no links change.
  • New: a question’s own negative marks can be set to 0 to override the quiz’s rate; leave the box blank to use the rate. Existing questions are unchanged.
  • New: marks and penalties keep four decimal places (for example 0.8571).
  • New: write a question in a second language (for example Hindi) alongside the first, and turn on partial marks for multiple-answer questions – both used by Exam Mode in Pro.
  • Fixed: a question that is only an image can be saved.

0.3.7

  • New: courses work on a fresh site with no LearnDash – create courses, lessons and quizzes straight away.
  • New: [turgee_courses] shows a free grid of your courses with lesson counts and each student’s progress; all courses are also listed at /courses/.
  • New: standalone mock tests. Tick “Open to every signed-in student” in a quiz’s settings and anyone signed in can take it from its page, without a course or enrolment. List them all on any page with [turgee_quizzes].
  • New: put a quiz straight into a course – a test between lessons or a final exam – with “Add quiz to course” in the course builder. Course-level quizzes brought over from LearnDash now show to students too.
  • New: switch negative marking on per quiz and set the share of marks lost for a wrong answer.
  • New: the plugin’s home screen lists every shortcode and what it shows.
  • Improved: the course and quiz builders are open when you add a new course or quiz, instead of folded away at the bottom of the editor.
  • Fixed: a new course starts as Free when Turgor Exam Engine Pro is not installed, so students can enrol straight away.
  • Fixed: after activation the plugin now opens its home screen as intended.
  • Improved: clearer, jargon-free wording across the Migration screen and settings – steps are now Check, Copy your content, Switch the site over, Protect your edits and Turn off LearnDash.
  • Renamed: Turgor LMS is now Turgor Exam Engine (slug turgor-exam-engine). Courses, students, quizzes and settings move across automatically the first time it runs. Shortcodes are now [turgee_…]; on a site that used the old [tg_…] names, those keep working.
  • Changed: negative marking and quiz time limits always work in this plugin; they no longer depend on Turgor Exam Engine Pro being active.
  • Changed: copy protection for lesson and quiz content now ships in Turgor Exam Engine Pro.
  • Changed: updates now come only from WordPress.org; the plugin no longer checks turgorlabs.com for updates.
  • Changed: the admin menu sits in its default position, and Pro features are described on one “Pro add-on” page instead of separate locked menu items.
  • Security: tightened nonce checks, input sanitizing and output escaping on every form and admin screen.

short_description: Mock tests and courses for WordPress: negative marking, timed papers in sections, random questions, live test windows and question analysis.
description:
Turgor Exam Engine is a full LMS for WordPress, built around competitive-exam style tests. Run mock tests with negative marking, timed papers in sections and numeric-range answers, and build the courses that lead up to them, all on your own WordPress site and database – not a hosted service.

Made for coaching institutes, test-series sellers and teachers preparing students for exams like SSC, IBPS, JEE, NEET, GATE and CSIR NET.

Exam engine

  • Eight question types: single choice, multiple choice, fill in the blank, free answer (which can accept a numeric range – an answer key of “6300..6400”, as GATE and IIT JAM publish), sorting, matching, rating scale and essay. Seven are marked automatically; essays wait on the Results screen for a teacher to mark.
  • Negative marking, with a per-question penalty where a paper needs one.
  • Standalone mock tests: open any quiz to every signed-in student from its own page, no course needed.
  • Timed papers split into named sections, with retake limits and question and answer shuffling. (A separate timer per section is part of Exam Mode in Turgor Exam Engine Pro.)
  • A question bank with categories, difficulty levels and topics: search it, filter it and edit any question, and every quiz that uses it changes with it.
  • A Results screen listing every attempt, where you mark essays, give a student their retakes back, or re-mark attempts after correcting an answer key.
  • Sitewide defaults for every setting, overridable on any single quiz.
  • A per-question review after submission, and a results chart students can see with [turgee_quiz_results].
  • Random questions: a section draws questions from a question-bank category, so every student gets a different paper.
  • Live tests with open and close times: nobody starts outside the window, and anyone still sitting the quiz is stopped at closing time.
  • Question analysis on Results: right, wrong and blank counts per question and the average time, hardest first.
  • Reading passages shared by several questions, and LaTeX formulae drawn as typeset maths.
  • Choose when students see the right answers: straight away, when no attempts are left, after the quiz closes, or never.

Courses

Build each course as an outline of sections, topics, lessons, sub-lessons and quizzes. Drag items into place or use the + buttons, create a lesson or quiz by typing its title, and set prerequisites and completion rules per course. Students see the same outline on the course page.

  • Drip content: a lesson or quiz opens a set number of days after access begins, and/or not before a date.
  • Assignments, marked with a mark and feedback, and lesson discussions using ordinary WordPress comments.
  • Lesson videos with chapters, a speed menu and resume.
  • Gutenberg blocks and shortcodes for course lists, quizzes, progress, results and sign-in.
  • Open, no-signup courses and one-click free enrollment.
  • A Quick start checklist and a one-click sample course to get a new site running.
  • An Instructor role that can mark essays and see results without being an administrator.

Already running LearnDash?

A guided import brings your courses, lessons, quizzes and enrolled students across, with verification tools that check the migration actually worked before you switch over – nothing is deleted or changed on your live site until you say so.

Want to sell what you build?

Turgor Exam Engine is free and complete on its own. Turgor Exam Engine Pro adds Exam Mode (the computer-based exam screen, with a timer per section and partial marks for multiple choice), WooCommerce and Google Play Billing checkout, bundled Products (and, when moving from LearnDash, bringing groups, bundles and WooCommerce products across, with checks that paid courses moved over correctly), class reports, certificates issued automatically on completion, copy protection for lesson and quiz content, and student feedback tools. Pro is one purchase that includes all of it, and it is never required: everything in Turgor Exam Engine works fully without it.

Requirements

  • PHP 8.1 or newer
  • WordPress 6.7 or newer

Third-party libraries

  • KaTeX 0.16.11, MIT License – draws formulae in questions. Bundled minified as assets/vendor/katex/katex.min.js and auto-render.min.js, with its stylesheet and fonts; the source is at https://github.com/KaTeX/KaTeX.
  • Chart.js 4.5.1, MIT License – draws the quiz-results chart. Bundled minified as assets/vendor/chart.umd.min.js; the unminified source is at https://github.com/chartjs/Chart.js.
